title: Hover hints, round two — the timing and the circled i

steps.path: The row of icons along the top of the window
steps.headline: Rest on one icon, then sweep along the row — is the timing right now?
steps.changed: Two changes, both yours. The first hint comes a little sooner than it did. And moving between neighbouring buttons is no longer instant: the next one waits a moment and fades in, instead of the bubble cutting from button to button.
steps.notice: Sweeping fast across the row should feel like one hint following you, not a strobe. Leave the row for about half a second and the next hover waits the full time again.
steps.risk: The fade is switched off entirely when Reduce Visual Effects is on, or when the system asks for less motion — so on those settings it will still cut.

steps.path: The Cost, In, Out, Cached, Reuse, Speed and lines chips
steps.headline: Click the small circled i on the chips — is this the right home for the long explanations?
steps.changed: Seven chips whose explanation was a whole sentence no longer hover at all. Each has a small circled i; clicking it opens the explanation, and it stays open until you click away. This is the answer you gave on the first deck, now built.
steps.notice: This pane deliberately shows a session with real figures, so those chips exist. In your own app they are switched off until you turn them on with the pencil at the right-hand end of the bar. The wording inside each bubble is word for word what the old grey box said — nothing was rewritten.
steps.risk: That is seven new marks on a bar that was already busy, and only one bubble can be open at a time.

steps.path: The row of sessions along the top, and the files drawer on the right
steps.headline: Hover a session name, the close crosses and the drawer icons — does anything look out of place?
steps.changed: The session row and the files drawer are converted too, which finishes the set you asked for: everything that is on screen all the time. Settings and the marketplace still use the grey box, as agreed.
steps.notice: A session name too long for its row shows the full name on hover, the way it always did — the box around it is the only difference. The drawer's icons along the top now name themselves.
steps.risk: The session row is narrow and its hints are the ones that fire most often, simply because the pointer crosses it on the way to everywhere else.
